There is a way around admin edits of user's opinions other than archives. Archives only work if you happened to have one ready. It also doesn't work for past comments made years ago.

We can use cryptographic signatures like the one you will see at the end of this post to verify that something was written by you. You can put the public key hash in your profile and the only way an admin could edit your comment would be to edit your public key hash as well which would invalidate all other comments you've made on a site.

I'm using bitcoin because private keys are short, signatures can be validated with only a hash of the public key, and GUI software exists in many forms that are easy for people to access.

If you don't use bitcoin you should get to know it.

Go to https://electrum.org/ and download a wallet software. I make a wallet separate from my money for signatures.

Go to the "Addresses" tab and right click the top address. Click "Edit Label" to label it "Signatures" just so you know that one address is the one you are doing signatures with. (For payment anonymity reasons most bitcoin wallets work with a library of addresses.)

Now go to "Tools" at the top and click "Sign/verify message". There you can enter the address you want to sign with as well as the message you want to sign and you will get something like what you see at the bottom.

You can and should place your address into your Voat profile signature, as I have. You can access that at https://voat.co/account/manage.

But what about formatting:

Voat uses markdown formatting as well does reddit. To make things easier on someone wanting to verify a comment you should sign the end product. Many times that is the same as what you enter. If you have used formatting tricks it may not. Hit preview and you should get something you can sign.

Now add <sub>Signature: My signature</sub> to the bottom.

Verifying uses the exact same toolset and I think you can figure it out.

Might I suggest gpg as an alternative to bitcoin (especially for those without bitcoin accounts)?

One would need to create a public/private key pair for themselves, then make their public key available (maybe at pgp.mit.edu/ or keybase.io/ ).

Signing messages are similar to how /u/bikergang_accountant does it, which would be something like

gpg --clearsign <message_filename>

(this would result in creating a new file "<message_filename>.asc" that has the signature).

Verifying messages requires having the public key of the signer but is done with:

gpg --verify <signed_message_filename>

A place to learn how to use gpg: https://gnupg.org/gph/en/manual.html

You can test verifying my post by getting my public key with

curl https://keybase.io/seodisparate/key.asc | gpg --import

then verify my message by downloading my signed post to a file and doing

gpg --verify <message_filename>

gpg will indicate with "Good Signature" if the signature is valid.

The issue with gpg signatures is the block of text with the clearsigned signature needs to be verified as-is, thus posts with clearsigned signatures on voat (or some other social media sites) need to be encapsulated in a code block, or separately linked to.
